title: June Clark and Ed Swayzee
summary: Holmes recalls trumpeters June Clark, who later boxed, and Ed Swayzee, a neat, clean player, but little detail about either.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well, while we're on various musicians, while we're on Duke Ellington, do you remember June Clark, who played with Ellington for a short time?
Well, I remember June Clark, but I don't remember him being with Ellington. I guess he had been. I remember June Clark...
He went into boxing.
Was he a trumpet player?
Yeah.
Yeah, June Clark, that's right. There was a June Cole, too, a bass player. Yeah, I remember June Clark.
Holmes (1/14) - 6
He became a second later to I think Sugar Ray Robinson or one of the boxers...
Yeah, something like that.
But he was in Ellington's band...
Yeah, I don't doubt it.
...just about the time when you came.

Yeah, way back. Yeah, June Clark. That's when Duke wasn't doing so good. I mean, you know, he had no big name then. Before the Cotton Club days he had a small group. They used to work the Kentucky Club. I don't know if June was down there with him or not, or Bubber Miley. I think June was there before Bubber Miley.
Yeah, I think so, too.
Bubber was with him when I came here -- with Duke. Yeah, I know June very well.
What about another trumpet player, Ed Swayzee? He's kind of early also.
Yeah, I know Swayzee. I'm trying to...
He was with Cab Calloway at one point.
Yeah. I knew him, but I don't remember him so well. I don't know nothin' that... You know what I mean.
He died early. He died in '35.
Yeah, nothin' outstanding about him. I mean, he was a very neat person, one of them things. But I
Holmes (1/14) - 7
don't remember no incidents or anything about him.
And he was with Chick Webb.

Yeah, he was a good trumpet player. That's all I can say. I can't even remember what he looked like, but I remember the name. And then Doc Cheatham...they reminded me of one another, you know. He was a good trumpeter, a clean trumpet player, you know what I mean, like Doc is. And another fellow named Mouse Randolph, he was a nice trumpet player, too. Them three always reminded me of one another -- Doc, Swayzee and Randolph.
